analysis.title: Hawks Circle As Soaring CPI Lifts The Dollar, Hammers Everything Else... AI Credit Cracks Wide-Open
key_insights: Hot core CPI on Oct 14 2026, broad-based rather than energy-only, pushed October rate-hike odds above 50% and December odds above 95% intraday before pulling back as stocks fell. 2027 still prices two more hikes.
Treasury yields spiked on the CPI print, led by the short end, then a bid returned as equities sold off and AI credit fears grew. The 10Y reversed its initial spike.
CoreWeave (CRWV) CDS closed +135bps. The credit market implies a 63% chance CRWV defaults within five years. CRWV shares fell about 15% by noon and its bonds trade in the $70s.

A Gartner report said 80% of NeoClouds will cease independent operations by 2030 if AI infrastructure spending continues. Gartner expects AI providers to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2026 and an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030, with enterprise and consumer AI revenue insufficient to support profitable returns on all of it.

NeoCloud and AI-adjacent equities sold off: DOCN -14%, HUT -10%, NBIS and IREN -9%, CIFR and APLD -8.7%, ORCL -9%. CRWV counts hyperscalers among its largest customers and Nvidia as an investor. NeoClouds sit in Nvidia's AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise segment, nearly half of its data-center revenue.

Credit stress is moving up the quality curve: CCC yields trade over 1000bps, IG and HY spreads are pushing back toward post-Iran-War wides, data-center bond spreads are widening, and tech credit has underperformed most.
NDX and RTY each fell about 2%, their worst day since June. AI lagged SPX ex-AI by 840bps this week. SOXX is down 7 days in a row. All US majors closed red and the Dow outperformed.
BofA's earnings miss dragged financials, with MS and STT also weak. The sector also faces AI exposure risks.

SPX has moved through 7,775-7,750, where SpotGamma puts the volatility trigger and where positive dealer gamma offers support. A sustained break leaves 7,700 (7,690) as the key level before gamma thins toward the 50DMA. VIX rose back above 17. Bloomberg's Michael Ball says the calm low-vol regime is at risk of breaking.

Equity volatility was cheap relative to rates and oil volatility, and the gap has now closed for SPX vol versus TLT vol. Unless SPX reclaims the broken support, dip-buying is likely to give way to weakness producing more weakness.

The dollar broke out of its 18-month range to its highest since May 2025. Gold fell 1% to support at $4,100, silver fell 6% to a two-month low, and Bitcoin broke below $82,000, trading as high-beta tech.

WTI rose above $96, a three-week high, after a cargo ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz following a strike and another freighter was hit. Dated Brent was near $130 on Tuesday, and Middle East-to-China freight is near a record of about $1.39 million a day.

European diesel has more than doubled this year, US retail diesel is near record highs, and US diesel is cited as a large driver of the hot CPI. The author warns it bodes poorly for the next CPI. The IEA warned fuels will stay under pressure next year.
US financial conditions have tightened notably over recent weeks, driven mainly by yields, and today's moves in yields, spreads and the dollar added to it.

BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky sees a 'Red October' risk if Mag7 falls along with rates, which he calls the pain trade (rates down, Nasdaq down). He also says odds favor a semis bounce soon, with today lining up as a bottom under the 2000 analogy, but the bounce would be one to sell before a more drawn-out decline.

Goldman's trading desk rated activity 6 out of 10, with franchise flows skewed 8.9% better for sale. Long-only investors skewed 19.5% and hedge funds 12.6% better for sale. SPY volume on Monday was the lowest in 23 years.
